Below is the CFTC Traders in Financial Futures report (futures-only) for 10-Year U.S. Treasury Note futures, contract market code 043602, for the week ending 25 August 2026. All figures are numbers of contracts.

Open interest (all contracts): 6,208,739

| Trader category | Long | Short | Spreading | Net | Net as % of OI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dealer / Intermediary | 163,799 | 744,106 | 198,300 | -580,307 | -9.35% |
| Asset Manager / Institutional | 3,282,567 | 690,495 | 829,594 | 2,592,072 | +41.75% |
| Leveraged Funds | 316,808 | 2,451,147 | 583,582 | -2,134,339 | -34.38% |
| Other Reportable | 285,119 | 226,495 | 11,698 | 58,624 | +0.94% |

Output of a supervised model of leveraged-fund positioning (model v2.0):

- Expected net position this week: -39.52% of open interest (approximate 90% range based on the model's past errors: -42.97% to -36.07%)
- Actual net position this week: -34.38% of open interest
- Residual (actual minus expected): +5.14% of open interest, larger in size than 98% of the model's past out-of-sample residuals

How to read the model output above (model v2.0). The model predicts the weekly CHANGE in leveraged funds' net position, as a share of open interest, from conditions observed in the same week: price returns, realised volatility, yield levels and curve shape, equity volatility, a funding-stress measure, the change in open interest, the change in Fed Treasury holdings, a quarter-end flag, and the previous week's net positions of all four trader categories in this contract and of leveraged funds in the 2-, 5- and 30-year contracts. The expected position is last week's actual position plus the predicted change. It is a statistical association, not a decomposition by strategy. Specifically:

- The residual is the part of this week's CHANGE the model did not predict, given where the position stood last week. It is not the unexplained part of the whole outstanding position, not a quantity of basis trading, and not a directional signal. It contains misspecification, omitted variables and data error as well as anything informative.
- The model assigns no share of any position to any motive. It cannot: the cash leg of a basis trade is not in this dataset, and none of its inputs measures the cash-futures basis.
- Out of sample (2012-11-27 to 2026-09-08, 720 weeks) the model explains about 7% of the variance of weekly positioning changes. Its typical error is 2.1 percentage points of open interest, and the residual correlates about 0.97 with the raw weekly change, so most of what you see in the residual is simply the raw change.
- The expected-position range is approximate: in past weeks it contained the actual position 91% of the time. A residual inside the range is within the model's ordinary error.

What does this positioning suggest about the Treasury market?
